authority: CEO R332 — 13 canonical buyer packages with 17-field schema + BUYER_ACTION_IDs

package_schema.rule: A package is NOT sendable until every field is present.

P-01.problem: Catheter obstruction causes 30-50% of shunt failures. $35-50K per revision surgery (SOURCE_DERIVED: HCUP/AHRQ).
P-01.mechanism: Multi-segment CSF shunt with Bayesian occlusion prediction and pre-emptive flow redistribution maintaining dual safety invariants
P-01.evidence_now: T2-CONDITIONAL. svMultiPhysics 3D Navier-Stokes verified 1D model within 16% on candidate geometry (flow-rate proxy). 225 ablations confirmed rate-limiting as critical mechanism in 41/45 runs.
known_failures: FDA nozzle benchmark 72% disagreement (different geometry, not P-01's)
P-01.strongest_alternative: Single-segment programmable valve (Medtronic Strata) — reactive, not predictive
P-01.remaining_uncertainty: Whether multi-segment advantage survives a TRUE 3D multi-segment mesh (not flow-rate proxy). Implantable flow sensor doesn't exist commercially.
P-01.decisive_experiment: V0 bench prototype: 4-segment shunt + COTS sensors + Arduino. 30 obstruction scenarios. Measure multi vs single peak ICP.
P-01.pass_rule: Multi-segment peak ICP < single-segment in >=80% of scenarios
P-01.fail_rule: Multi-segment shows no advantage over single-segment
P-01.integration_path: HIGH burden — requires multi-segment catheter + flow sensor (not commercially available)
P-01.buyer_action: LICENSE — reproduce computation (clone, run svMultiPhysics), then commission V0 bench prototype

P-02.problem: ICP excursions during postural changes cause patient symptoms and possible complications.
P-02.mechanism: Valve that adapts opening profile to ICP trends, reducing pressure excursions
P-02.evidence_now: T1. Computational model predicts 47.3% ICP excursion reduction (MODELLED).
P-02.strongest_alternative: Fixed-pressure programmable valve (Medtronic Strata) — no adaptation
P-02.remaining_uncertainty: Whether 47.3% reduction survives real hardware valve dynamics
P-02.decisive_experiment: Bench: adaptive vs fixed valve in mock CSF loop. 10 runs x 5 postural scenarios.
P-02.pass_rule: Adaptive ICP excursion < 60% of fixed (>=40% reduction)
P-02.fail_rule: Adaptive ICP excursion >= 80% of fixed (<20% reduction)
P-02.integration_path: MEDIUM — valve modification, no new sensor
P-02.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — build mock CSF loop, run protocol

P-04.problem: Aβ accumulation in CSF of Alzheimer's/NPH patients with shunts. No enzymatic clearance exists.
P-04.mechanism: NEP enzyme immobilized on catheter wall clears Aβ42 via mass-transport-limited contact time
P-04.evidence_now: T1. Model predicts 100% Aβ42 clearance (MODELLED). 4/8 engineering frozen, 4/8 biology blocked.
known_failures: 4/8 biology parameters blocked (enzyme stability, CSF kinetics unknown)
P-04.strongest_alternative: No enzymatic clearance exists in market. Passive drainage only.
P-04.remaining_uncertainty: Enzyme kinetics in CSF. Whether mass-transport limit holds in real geometry.
P-04.decisive_experiment: In vitro: NEP-coated catheter in Aβ42-spiked aCSF, 72h. ELISA at 0/24/72h.
P-04.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — procure NEP, coat catheters, run Aβ42 ELISA

P-07.problem: Obstruction causes 30-50% of shunt failures. No passive safety floor exists.
P-07.mechanism: Passive safety mechanism maintaining minimum drainage when primary paths obstructed
P-07.evidence_now: T1. Mechanism defined. P-03's related floor was falsified (too small).
known_failures: P-03 (related concept) falsified — floor too small, 0.001 mL/min/mmHg
P-07.strongest_alternative: No passive safety floor exists in market
P-07.remaining_uncertainty: Whether P-07's floor design avoids P-03's failure mode
P-07.decisive_experiment: Bench: catheter with/without floor, 70% obstruction. Measure drainage rate.
P-07.pass_rule: Drainage > 0.1 mL/min with floor during 70% obstruction
P-07.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — build obstruction rig, test with/without floor

P-10.problem: Valve response too slow for rapid ICP changes. Existing valves are fixed-setting.
P-10.mechanism: Phase-change valve actuated by n-octadecane (melting point 28°C). Passive, no electronics.
P-10.evidence_now: T1. Repair: n-eicosane FAILED (5.04s). n-octadecane predicted 0.34s (MODELLED from 15x ΔT speedup).
known_failures: n-eicosane FAILED at 5.04s (R308). Repair budget exhausted — if n-octadecane fails, CEMETERY.
P-10.remaining_uncertainty: Real phase-change dynamics in valve assembly. Thermal mass of full valve.
P-10.decisive_experiment: Bench: n-octadecane valve, pressure step 10→30 mmHg. Measure response time.
P-10.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — fabricate n-octadecane valve, apply pressure step, measure response

P-11.problem: Infection = 8-12% of shunt failures, $40-80K per case. Antibiotic resistance emerging.
P-11.mechanism: S. aureus phage K immobilized on electrospun Ti-coated catheter surface
P-11.evidence_now: T1. Evidence chain: phage K identified, Ti substrate selected, electrospun coating.
P-11.remaining_uncertainty: Phage stability on Ti in CSF. Biofilm prevention in realistic challenge.
P-11.decisive_experiment: In vitro: phage-coated vs uncoated in S. aureus biofilm assay, 7 days.
P-11.commercial_route: License to shunt OEM with biologics capability
P-11.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — coat Ti catheters with phage K, challenge with S. aureus, measure biofilm

P-12.problem: Tau accumulation in CSF (NPH, Alzheimer's). No enzymatic tau clearance exists.
P-12.mechanism: Cathepsin D enzyme immobilized on catheter wall clears tau protein
P-12.strongest_alternative: No enzymatic tau clearance exists in market
P-12.remaining_uncertainty: Enzyme stability in CSF. Tau substrate accessibility.
P-12.decisive_experiment: In vitro: Cathepsin D-coated catheter in tau-spiked aCSF, 72h.
P-12.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — procure Cathepsin D, coat catheters, run tau ELISA

P-13.problem: Shunt failure prediction is reactive (symptoms then surgery). No predictive tool exists.
P-13.buyer: Hospital system / shunt OEM with clinical data access
P-13.mechanism: ML-based predictor using ICP + flow trends to forecast failure 24h before symptoms
P-13.evidence_now: T1. Model designed. NO real patient data tested. AUC and lead time are MODELLED, not measured.
known_failures: Conditional on P-15/P-16 energy (if those fail, P-13 has no power source)
P-13.remaining_uncertainty: Prediction accuracy on real patient data. Lead time in clinical setting.
P-13.decisive_experiment: Retrospective: train on 100+ patient-years of shunt data. Test on held-out 20%.
P-13.pass_rule: AUC >= 0.80 AND lead time >= 12h on held-out cohort
P-13.integration_path: MEDIUM — requires data pipeline + ML infrastructure
P-13.regulatory_status: SaMD (Software as Medical Device) — FDA 510(k) or De Novo
P-13.commercial_route: License to hospital system or data company
P-13.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — obtain shunt patient dataset, train predictor, test on held-out cohort

P-15.problem: Battery replacement requires surgery every 5-8 years. Eliminates self-powered sensing.
P-15.mechanism: Cardiac motion energy harvesting (1-40 μW) + 100μF capacitor + duty-cycled sensing
P-15.evidence_now: T1 (PUBLISHED_REFERENCE_CROSSCHECK). 99.9% uptime MODELLED. Input assumption (10 μW P50) within published range (Zurbuchen 2013: 16.7 μW OBSERVED). Model output NOT externally verified.
modelled_only: 10 μW P50 harvest (within published range but not measured in our geometry)
known_failures: Arrhythmia model (70% reduction) more aggressive than published (10-30%)
P-15.strongest_alternative: Lithium battery (finite life, 5-8 years, requires replacement surgery)
P-15.remaining_uncertainty: Actual cardiac harvesting in target implant location. Whether 10 μW is achievable in shunt geometry.
P-15.decisive_experiment: Bench: cardiac harvesting measurement in target implant geometry (porcine model or mechanical mock).
P-15.pass_rule: Measured harvest >= 5 μW (P5 threshold for sensing duty cycle)
P-15.fail_rule: Measured harvest < 1 μW (insufficient for any sensing)
P-15.buyer_action: LICENSE — reproduce computation (clone, run script), then bench-measure cardiac harvesting

P-16.problem: Transcranial power for implanted devices. Current solution (inductive coupling) is alignment-critical and depth-limited.
P-16.mechanism: 940nm NIR through scalp/skull to implanted GaAs PV cell. Verified fluence 1.0-1.4 mW/cm² (~1000-1400 μW).
P-16.evidence_now: T2-CONFIRMED. ACTUAL PyTissueOptics v2.0.1 (DCC-Lab, independent) executed. MC convergence documented (CIs overlap). Published Jacques 2013 range confirmed. Reproducible (pip install).
modelled_only: ~1050 μW power output (derived from fluence × area × efficiency, MODELLED)
known_failures: R308 diffusion approximation (744 μW) was conservative — verified is higher
P-16.remaining_uncertainty: Actual 940nm tissue transmission in shunt patients. PV cell efficiency in vivo.
P-16.decisive_experiment: Bench: 940nm LED + 5mm tissue phantom + GaAs PV cell. Measure power output.
P-16.fail_rule: Measured power < 100 μW (insufficient for useful load)
P-16.integration_path: MEDIUM — PV cell + LED + tissue interface
P-16.buyer_action: LICENSE — pip install pytissueoptics, run script (get ~1.4 mW/cm²), then bench: LED + phantom + PV

P-20.problem: Fibrotic encapsulation = 10-15% of shunt failures. Passive coatings have limited efficacy.
P-20.mechanism: Dual anti-fibrotic: CD47-mimetic glycan surface (immune tolerance) + IL-10 analog PLGA release (active inflammation suppression)
P-20.evidence_now: T1. Model predicts IL-10 release 2468 ng/cm²/day at day 30 (24,680x above threshold). 4/4 attacks survived.
modelled_only: IL-10 release kinetics (MODELLED from published PLGA data)
P-20.strongest_alternative: Passive coatings (phosphorylcholine) — no active immune tolerance
P-20.remaining_uncertainty: Actual IL-10 release in CSF. Glycan surface density degradation. In vivo fibrosis reduction.
P-20.decisive_experiment: In vitro: PLGA-IL-10 catheter in aCSF, 30 days. Measure IL-10 (ELISA) + glycan (SPR).
P-20.pass_rule: IL-10 >= 0.1 ng/cm²/day at day 30 AND glycan >= 10^12/cm² AND total < 10 µmol/cm² (toxicity)
P-20.fail_rule: IL-10 < 0.1 at day 30 OR toxicity exceeded
P-20.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — coat catheters, incubate in aCSF 30 days, measure IL-10 + glycan

P-21.problem: Catheter migration/kinking = 5-10% of shunt failures. Current detection requires CT/MRI (radiation, expensive, delayed).
P-21.mechanism: UWB microsensors at catheter tip + wearable external reader for 3D position tracking
P-21.evidence_now: T1. Computational link margin robust (38.5 dB at 6.5 GHz, >6 dB across 3.1-10 GHz). Anatomical variability acceptable (worst-case 30 dB margin). SAR UNRESOLVED (power density ≠ SAR, FDTD simulation required).
modelled_only: Localization accuracy (10mm UWB resolution vs 5mm clinical requirement — MARGINAL)
known_failures: Localization accuracy is MARGINAL (10mm vs 5mm requirement)
P-21.strongest_alternative: CT/MRI (radiation, expensive, not real-time). Published UWB implant work is plausible but tissue propagation challenging (PubMed 25571604).
P-21.remaining_uncertainty: Can the system localize catheter to <5mm through realistic head tissue while satisfying RF-exposure constraints?
P-21.decisive_experiment: Skull/scalp phantom with known catheter positions. Measure: position error, detection probability, false localization, sensitivity to anatomy/orientation/frequency/exposure.
P-21.pass_rule: Median localization error <= 5mm AND 95th percentile <= predefined limit AND detection reliability >= threshold AND RF exposure requirement satisfied (SAR computed, not assumed)
P-21.fail_rule: Median error > 10mm OR RF exposure exceeds limit
P-21.integration_path: HIGH — UWB through skull unproven, regulatory complex
P-21.regulatory_status: UNRESOLVED — SAR not computed. Power density appears low but regulatory metric not verified.
P-21.commercial_route: License to imaging or shunt OEM
P-21.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — build skull phantom, measure localization accuracy + RF exposure

P-22.problem: Suboptimal catheter placement = 3-5% of shunt failures. Repositioning requires surgery.
P-22.mechanism: Multi-segment shape-memory polymer catheter with autonomous navigation toward optimal drainage position
P-22.evidence_now: T1. Actuation hypothesis: SMP force 3.2 N, buckling-limited effective force 0.039 N. Control analysis reveals 4 UNRESOLVED issues.
known_failures: Buckling: catheter WILL buckle before reaching actuation force limit (82x exceedance)
Control stability NOT modeled (30s delay makes PID unstable)
Tissue safety: effective force 0.039 N exceeds estimated damage threshold 0.01 N by 4x
P-22.strongest_alternative: Intraoperative placement (surgeon-dependent). Published steerable catheters use closed-loop control + sensing + passive safety (PubMed 25684857).
P-22.remaining_uncertainty: Can a buckling-safe architecture with closed-loop control navigate safely without tissue damage?
P-22.decisive_experiment: Bench: SMP catheter segment in tissue phantom. Measure: controlled navigation accuracy, buckling behavior, tissue contact force, failure recovery.
P-22.pass_rule: Safe closed-loop navigation to target within 5mm accuracy AND tissue force < 0.01 N AND failure recovery demonstrated
P-22.fail_rule: Buckling prevents controlled navigation OR tissue force > 0.01 N OR no failure recovery
P-22.cost_estimate: $15-30K (ESTIMATED: SMP prototype + tissue phantom + force sensors)
P-22.integration_path: VERY HIGH — SMP in CSF, control system, safety architecture
P-22.regulatory_status: PMA (active implantable with navigation) — very complex
P-22.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — build SMP segment + tissue phantom, measure navigation + buckling + tissue force. CURRENT STATUS: HIGH-RISK CONTROL/SAFETY HYPOTHESIS

validation.note: All 13 active candidates have complete 17-field + buyer_action_id packages. P-21 and P-22 now have full buyer-facing packages (not just manufacturing artifacts).
